Changelog

flexCountReg 0.1.3 (development)

tidymodels and broom

  • tidy(), glance() and augment() methods, using the generics package (re-exported, so library(flexCountReg) provides them). tidy() returns the standard broom columns plus a component column (mean, distribution, underreporting, random-parameter and heterogeneity parameters), with conf.int and exponentiate (incidence rate ratios for the mean model). tidy() now works for every estimator. broom is no longer a dependency.
  • New count_reg() parsnip model with a "flexCountReg" engine, registered when parsnip is loaded (parsnip is suggested, not required). The count family is a main argument and can be tuned with count_family() (a dials parameter). Case weights are passed as frequency weights.
  • predict() accepts new_data (the tidymodels name) as well as newdata.
  • Standard errors are NA (instead of 0) when the estimated variance is negative, which happens for weakly identified parameters.

Breaking changes and changed results

  • summary() now returns a summary.flexCountReg object with a print method (coefficients with z statistics, the standard-error type, log-likelihood, AIC, BIC, N and panels, convergence, and a likelihood-ratio test against Poisson for countreg() models). Use summary(m)$coefficients for the coefficient matrix, or tibble::as_tibble(summary(m)) for the tibble that summary() returned before. The offset is shown as a note, not as a coefficient row.

  • Fitted objects have class c(<estimator>, "flexCountReg"), with <estimator> one of countreg, countreg_rp, renb, poislind_re, repois and negmultinom. The unused S4 class definition is removed. The training data are stored once (obj$data); obj$model$data is gone.

  • regCompTest() with two models now treats the model with fewer parameters as the restricted model (before: the one with the higher log-likelihood), errors when the models were fit to different numbers of observations, and warns when the restricted model has the higher log-likelihood. Its base and null models use the same rows, offset and weights as the fitted model, and McFadden’s R^2 uses an intercept-only model of the same family for countreg() models. regCompTable() uses the same definitions.

  • cor2cov() stops (instead of warning and returning NULL) on invalid input, and checks that C is a symmetric correlation matrix.

  • margEffTable() includes by default the variables of the underreporting, random-parameter and heterogeneity formulas (and the dispersion formulas of PLN and PLL models), which also change the expected value.

  • Probit underreporting now uses P(reported) = pnorm(z’g), the same sign convention as logit (a positive coefficient means more likely to be reported). Previously probit used 1 - pnorm(z’g), so probit coefficients had the opposite sign. Refit probit models to update them; predict() on probit fits made with earlier versions still uses the old convention.

  • countreg(): giving an offset both with offset() in the formula and with the offset argument is now an error. Before, a formula offset() was silently ignored.

  • countreg(): an invalid method, family, stderr or underreport_family is now an error instead of a warning or a silent fallback. dis_param_formula_1/_2 given for a parameter the family does not have is an error.

  • countreg() starting values now come from a Poisson GLM that uses the same rows, offset and weights as the model, so results can differ slightly (usually closer to the optimum).

  • predict() errors when an offset column used in fitting is missing from newdata, instead of silently setting the offset to 0.

  • countreg.rp(): heterogeneity in means now follows Wood and Gayah (2025, Eq. 2). Each random parameter has its own coefficient for each variable in het_mean_formula (named HetMean:<parameter>:<variable>), and the effect is additive (on the log scale for lognormal parameters; multiplicative for gamma parameters, whose mean must stay positive). Previously a single coefficient vector multiplied every random parameter’s mean. Estimates from models with het_mean_formula change; saved fits still predict with their original specification.

  • countreg.rp(): uniform random parameters now span mu +/- St.Dev (draws 2u - 1), matching the paper and the Exact prediction. Previously the draws spanned mu +/- St.Dev/2, so estimated uniform St.Dev values are now half as large. predict() converts saved uniform fits automatically (with a one-time message).

  • countreg.rp(): rpardists is matched to the random parameters by name (not position) and validated. An intercept in both formula and rpar_formula (an unidentified model) is an error; the intercept implied by rpar_formula is not a random parameter unless the fixed formula has no intercept. An invalid panel_id, family or method is an error.

  • countreg.rp(): weights now weight the panel log-likelihood (frequency weights for whole panels) instead of each row’s probability.

  • countreg.rp(): the mixing distribution of PLN, PGE, PLL and PW families uses its own Halton dimension; it previously reused the first random parameter’s draws, which made the two perfectly correlated.

  • predict(method = "Exact") returns Inf (with a warning) where the expected value does not exist: lognormal random parameters with a positive x, and gamma random parameters beyond the domain of their moment generating function. The lognormal formula is documented as a Laplace approximation.

  • renb() and poisLind.re() require group_var, and the panels always come from it (a panel_id column in data is no longer used instead). Bootstrapped standard errors resample whole panels instead of rows.

  • pplindLnorm(), qplindLnorm() and rplindLnorm() convert lambda to mean consistently with dplindLnorm() (the extra exp(sigma^2 / 2) factor is removed).

  • dpLnorm(), dpinvgaus(), dpinvgamma(), dplind() and dgwar() are vectorized directly instead of through Vectorize(). Off-support x gives 0 with a warning, and invalid parameters give NaN with a warning.

Bug fixes

  • countreg(): offsets given with offset() in the formula are now used in estimation and prediction.
  • countreg(): bootstrapped standard errors are matched to parameters by name. They were previously sorted alphabetically and printed against the wrong coefficients. Failed bootstrap replicates are counted and reported.
  • countreg(): all data (main formula, dis_param_formula_1/2, underreport_formula, offset and weights) are taken from one set of complete cases, so missing values no longer misalign rows. The number of removed rows is reported.
  • countreg(): stderr = "robust" and stderr = "boot" now set the stored standard errors and covariance matrix ($model$vcov, $model$vcov_type), which summary() and margEffTable() use. stderr = "boot" without bootstraps uses 200 replicates. The SE type is stored in $model$stderr.
  • countreg(): parameter values where a distribution’s density fails no longer abort the fit; the likelihood returns NA so the optimizer steps back.
  • countreg(): start.vals must have one value per parameter, and named values are matched by name. $model$converged is now set (with a warning when the optimizer does not report convergence).
  • predict() returns one value per row of newdata, in order, with NA for rows with missing values, instead of recycling shorter vectors. Training factor levels and contrasts are used, so newdata can contain a subset of levels. Coefficients are matched by name.
  • predict() sums multiple offset columns and uses formula offsets.
  • predict() for PLL models now includes the exp(sigma^2 / 2) lognormal mean factor, as it already did for PLN.
  • countreg.rp() now stores its offset, so predict() uses it. Simulated predictions now include heterogeneity in means and variances.

Bug fixes (distributions and panel models)

  • dpinvgaus() and dpinvgamma() are computed on the log scale, so they no longer return Inf or NaN at large counts (e.g. y > 85 with mu = 2, eta = 0.5).
  • r-functions (rpLnorm(), rplind(), rplindLnorm(), rplindGamma(), rpge(), rcom(), rgp1(), rgp2()) accept vector parameters, as needed for simulation from fitted models. Mixture families draw the mixing variable per observation.
  • q-functions no longer loop forever at p = 1 (they return Inf), return NaN for p outside [0, 1], and no longer recompute the CDF at every step.
  • dplind(lambda = ) uses lambda (it previously ignored it).
  • dgp1() and dgp2() are vectorized, and for underdispersed values the normalizing constant is summed only where the probability is not negligible. Near phi = 0 (or alpha = 0) from below the old code summed up to millions of terms per observation, so GP1/GP2 fits could run for hours (for example the GP1 example in ?countreg, which now takes under a second).
  • The RENB likelihood computes log-gamma differences without cancellation for large means. Previously the likelihood was overstated far from the optimum, and optimizers such as BFGS could converge to meaningless estimates.
  • poisLind.re() starts from a moment estimate of theta instead of an undocumented formula.
  • renb() and poisLind.re() use the same data preparation as countreg(): missing values are removed consistently, formula offsets work (giving both a formula offset and offset is an error), and starting values use the offset.
  • countreg.rp() uses the shared data preparation (formula offsets, missing values, numeric weights), starts gamma random parameters from a positive mean, averages panel likelihoods over draws on the log scale, and reports convergence.
  • predict(method = "Exact") for countreg.rp() includes heterogeneity in means and variances.

Documentation

  • Corrected the Generalized Poisson parameter restrictions, the parameter table in ?countreg (PGE, Sichel), the Poisson-Lindley-Lognormal mean and parameter descriptions, the RENB density, the Sichel reference (Zou, Lord and Zhang, 2012) and several typos. ?countreg no longer claims that an LR test is printed; see regCompTest().
  • ?countreg.rp documents each random-parameter distribution’s scale, the heterogeneity specification and the lognormal caveat.
  • ?washington_roads describes the panel structure; the Rollover label in the data is corrected. The README function list is corrected and completed.

Other changes

  • Dependencies: broom, dplyr, modelr, purrr, stringr and tidyr are no longer used; generics is added. Whole-namespace imports are replaced by importFrom(). lamW stays in Suggests (its uses in qlindley() and lognormal random-parameter predictions are checked with rlang::check_installed()); dials and parsnip are added to Suggests.

  • rlindley() draws from the gamma mixture form directly (no longer needs lamW) and no longer warns for every whole-number n.

  • src/Makevars and src/Makevars.win are removed (no OpenMP or BLAS is used), so SystemRequirements: GNU make is dropped.

  • Added an R CMD check GitHub Actions workflow (including a job with only the hard dependencies installed) and a grouped pkgdown reference index. Removed the commented-out tests/testthat/test-all.R and a duplicated test.

  • The poilog engine is checked with rlang::check_installed().

  • msg1 and .dpge_one are no longer exported. The hand-maintained Collate field is removed.

New features

  • Zero-inflated and hurdle models for every countreg() family, through the new zero_formula and zero_type arguments (checked against pscl::zeroinfl() and pscl::hurdle()).

  • predict(type = "prob") (probabilities of each count), randomized quantile residuals (residuals(type = "quantile")) and rootogram().

  • Analytic gradients for the Poisson, NB1 and NB2 families (with or without a dispersion formula), used by the gradient-based optimizers and by robust standard errors.

  • Internally, each count family is defined once in a family registry (R/families.R), which makes adding a family a one-file change.

  • predict(method = "Individual") (alias "EB") for countreg.rp() models now computes Empirical Bayes observation-specific predictions following Wood and Gayah (2025), weighting each draw by the likelihood of the unit’s observed outcomes. Previously it returned the simulated predictions. eb_type = "mean" returns the conditional mean instead of plugging in the conditional coefficients; the conditional coefficients and their standard deviations are returned as attributes.

  • predict() gains type = c("response", "true", "prob_reported", "link") for countreg() models.

  • countreg() accepts weights as a numeric vector as well as a column name.

Deprecations

  • predict(object, data = ...) is deprecated; use newdata.
  • print.level in renb(), poisLind.re() and repois() is deprecated; use verbose. panel_id in countreg.rp() is deprecated; use group_var. The old names still work, with a once-per-session warning.

Methods and API consistency

  • New methods for all models: coef(), vcov(), logLik(), nobs(), fitted(), residuals() (response and, for countreg(), Pearson), confint(), formula(), terms() and print(). AIC(), BIC() and update() now work. For panel models, logLik() reports the number of panels as its nobs, so BIC() uses the number of independent units.
  • simulate() draws responses from fitted countreg() models (all families, including underreporting).
  • Every estimator stores one covariance matrix (vcov()), and renb(), poisLind.re(), repois() and countreg.rp() gain stderr = c("normal", "robust", "boot"). Robust standard errors of panel models are clustered by panel; bootstraps resample whole panels. countreg.rp() gains bootstraps.
  • All estimators gain keep_data; keep_data = FALSE does not store the training data.
  • countreg_rp() and poislind_re() are snake_case names for countreg.rp() and poisLind.re().
  • repois() predictions work (its linear-predictor coefficients were truncated to one value), and its likelihood returns one value per cluster.
  • For fitted models, AIC() and BIC() replace myAIC() and myBIC().
